scope: The 50 unique Linear tickets audited in screen-reader.spec.ts before this consolidation.
policy: Every ticket must resolve to at least one relevant test. Partial mappings are not proof of the original remedy. Removing Guidepup coverage requires replacement browser evidence and explicit AT limitations.

browserRun.scope: Only the browser cases replacing the audited candidates. No full suite or Guidepup execution.
browserRun.command: PORT=3001 MONGODB_URL=<isolated test database> pnpm test:e2e a11y --grep 'default login logo|expose required state without naming|identify the .* row on its drag control|describe pickup movement drop|drop a keyboard-dragged|active sort direction on relationship table|selected folder as the current|visit every theme option|current locale and popup state|name version table per-page|live-preview zoom name, expansion|selected Add Blocks option by name|disabled Paste or Replace|Welcome and the signed-in account|navigate LLM instructions tabs|name LLM instructions editors' --workers=1

verification.screenReaderRun: Not run on this laptop; do not infer AT success from browser assertions.

outstanding: PYLD-3671 and PYLD-3678: current assertions permit a native label stop, unlike the original single-stop requirement. Native WebKit baseline also repeats labels. These remain partial coverage.

PYLD-3580: DOM keyboard-focus persistence is fixed by a temporary branch-local Sonner patch and four browser checks pass. Virtual-cursor-only persistence remains unverified; replace the root patch with a published-package solution before the final PR.
Reported NVDA/Chrome failures require that platform's evidence; this branch's default Windows Guidepup project uses Firefox.
NVDA browse-mode tests and screen-reader cursor containment must retain AT evidence.
Guidepup queue hazards removed from retained direction/version/widget captures; remote AT verification is still required.
Further review found partial original-scenario coverage for PYLD-3699/PYLD-3730 (selected-locale cursor grouping) and PYLD-3642 (widget frame versus drag handle).

remainingScreenReaderReview.scope: Static review covered all 37 expanded cases at commit 203e115335. Four were subsequently retired with explicit browser replacements and recorded manual limits; cases tracks the 33 remaining cases and retiredCases preserves all four decisions.
remainingScreenReaderReview.interpretation: Retain means the observable outcome justifies AT evidence, not that the test has passed or proves conformance. Strengthen means current assertions have a concrete false-pass, false-failure, scope, or cursor-start risk.

platformInventory.note: On macOS the five NVDA-only cases are skipped; they are not passes.

sharedRisks.finding: The helper returns a match from current item text OR last spoken phrase and resets to web-content root first. A matching prior/context phrase does not prove the cursor reached the named control.

The installed adapter exits focus mode, clicks/blurs the body, and navigates to page top. It establishes browse mode, but can change an already-open menu; calling it after opening an options list is not neutral.
NVDA itemText returns lastSpokenPhrase; it is not independent accessibility-node identity evidence.

This helper still sets DisableAutologin on all page requests. External font requests can receive that custom header and trigger CORS failures; this is a setup hazard, not proof of a password accessibility failure.
The Windows project uses Firefox, while many source reports specify NVDA with Chrome. Track exact reported-platform verification separately.
Eighty blind steps per modal can be slow and can pass without progress. The media test performs this for two modals; cursor progress and scope must be established.

cases.test: should announce associated labels for the duplicate locale checkboxes
cases.title: should announce associated labels for the duplicate locale checkboxes

cases.test: should announce the associated label for the deletion checkbox
cases.title: should announce the associated label for the deletion checkbox

cases.test: should announce table cell text once without conflicting sort commands
cases.title: should announce table cell text once without conflicting sort commands
cases.finding: Duplicate cell readout and conflicting sort speech are actual AT outcomes. The expected title is checked once in spoken output, but only one fixture cell is sampled.
cases.next: Keep focused speech coverage; verify on NVDA/Chrome as reported, rather than inferring it from VoiceOver or NVDA/Firefox.

cases.test: should communicate removed version text while browsing the comparison
cases.title: should communicate removed version text while browsing the comparison
cases.finding: The test aggregates speech from up to 30 stops and separately checks removed text and a deletion word. Those can come from different stops; navigation is not bounded to the older comparison side.
cases.next: Require removal meaning associated with the target removed text/current comparison side, without depending on a specific screen-reader pronunciation of strikethrough.

cases.test: should announce the deletion dialog before background page content
cases.title: should announce the deletion dialog before background page content
cases.finding: The report concerns announcement order. The assertion instead rejects a short list of background words anywhere in the captured speech; it does not compare the first dialog announcement with an actual background sentinel.
cases.next: Check the initial relevant announcement and dialog arrival on the reported NVDA platform; distinguish background preceding the dialog from legitimate later context.

cases.test: should announce a selected locale as one grouped item with its state
cases.title: should announce a selected locale as one grouped item with its state
cases.finding: Counting English once in one focus capture proves neither one virtual-cursor stop nor grouping relative to the unselected locale. The selected/not-disabled state does have browser and focus-speech evidence.
cases.next: Retain browser state coverage for PYLD-3700; verify actual browse stops for PYLD-3699 and the grouping portion of PYLD-3730.

cases.test: should drop the ${kind} row with the screen reader active
cases.title: should drop the Array row with the screen reader active
cases.finding: The original failure depends on the screen reader being active when moving/dropping a row. DOM-only keyboard dragging is complementary, not an equivalent replacement.
cases.next: Keep both Array and Blocks cases; confirm the intended AT mode and key handling before diagnosing a failure.

cases.test: should drop the ${kind} row with the screen reader active
cases.title: should drop the Blocks row with the screen reader active
cases.finding: The original failure depends on the screen reader being active when moving/dropping a row. DOM-only keyboard dragging is complementary, not an equivalent replacement.
cases.next: Keep both Array and Blocks cases; confirm the intended AT mode and key handling before diagnosing a failure.

cases.test: should lift a dashboard widget with Space while NVDA is active
cases.title: should lift a dashboard widget with Space while NVDA is active
cases.finding: PYLD-3642 starts with keyboard focus on the widget frame and Space incorrectly opening Edit. This test directly focuses the separate drag handle before Space.
cases.next: Test the keyboard path from the frame and document the revised frame/handle interaction contract; a handle-only pass does not prove the literal reported trigger.

cases.test: should reach widget edit size and remove controls with the VoiceOver cursor
cases.title: should reach widget edit size and remove controls with the VoiceOver cursor
cases.finding: Actual VoiceOver cursor access to widget controls is appropriate. The helper resets to the page root for three searches, which loses the widget anchor and can match another widget or exhaust a large traversal.
cases.next: Anchor traversal before the target controls, bound it to the added widget, and verify each visited item before activation.

cases.test: should not expose an invisible loading object after relationship drawer content
cases.title: should not expose an invisible loading object after relationship drawer content
cases.finding: The synthetic end marker is appended inside the drawer. An unknown object immediately after the drawer could be excluded by that boundary. A blacklist of loading/unknown/unlabeled strings also misses an empty stop.
cases.next: Confirm the reported last-field-to-next-item transition in NVDA and place the scan boundary after the relevant possible loading object, without repairing the accessibility tree under test.

cases.test: should allow the NVDA browse cursor to exit Lexical editors in both directions
cases.title: should allow the NVDA browse cursor to exit Lexical editors in both directions
cases.finding: The report concerns NVDA browse-mode escape from both editors. The test explicitly exits focus mode, navigates both directions, and checks outside boundaries; ordinary Tab tests do not prove this.
cases.next: Keep the reported-platform check; verify boundary matches identify outside content, and diagnose cursor state before extending step limits.

cases.test: should omit hidden Lexical controls from screen-reader navigation
cases.title: should omit hidden Lexical controls from screen-reader navigation
cases.finding: The negative scan terminates at broad text/edit or Add item matches. It can finish before all relevant hidden controls are traversed or confuse an editor-local item with outside content.
cases.next: Use explicit outside-editor boundaries and demonstrate the relevant region was traversed; keep actual virtual-cursor evidence.

cases.test: should expose validation errors next to their fields
cases.title: should expose validation errors next to their fields
cases.finding: The retained document case checks the original document-submission reading-order report. The helper still starts from DOM focus without first verifying the AT cursor position.
cases.next: Verify the AT starting field before the adjacency scan; login coverage is now browser plus recorded manual VoiceOver evidence.

cases.test: should contain screen-reader traversal in bulk-upload and image-edit dialogs
cases.title: should contain screen-reader traversal in bulk-upload and image-edit dialogs
cases.finding: The fixed 40-forward/40-backward scans do not require progress or distinct expected controls. A cursor repeating Add files or Crop can pass the positive/negative word checks. Background-name blacklists can also reject legitimate modal content.
cases.next: Require progress through known modal boundaries and controls, then test confinement in both directions. If unreliable, retain browser isolation checks plus explicit manual virtual-cursor verification.

cases.test: should contain screen-reader traversal in the nested folder-location modal
cases.title: should contain screen-reader traversal in the nested folder-location modal
cases.finding: Like the media scan, this can pass while repeating one in-modal item and does not demonstrate traversal through the modal.
cases.next: Require distinct expected locations and bounded forward/reverse coverage; retain manual AT containment evidence if automation cannot reliably reproduce it.

cases.test: should move the screen-reader cursor into the add-widget drawer upon opening
cases.title: should move the screen-reader cursor into the add-widget drawer upon opening
cases.finding: The test captures opening the real drawer and checks the screen-reader item immediately, which addresses automatic AT cursor entry rather than merely DOM focus.
cases.next: Keep this representative modal-entry scenario; browser isolation/focus checks remain complementary.

cases.test: should move the screen-reader cursor into Copy to locale from the overflow menu
cases.title: should move the screen-reader cursor into Copy to locale from the overflow menu
cases.finding: The report concerns opening a drawer from an overflow menu resetting AT focus. The test captures that exact transition and rejects the previous menu/page context.
cases.next: Keep; inspect actual current item and target drawer readiness when diagnosing, without resetting the cursor after opening.

cases.test: should expose one screen-reader stop for the Copy to locale select
cases.title: should expose one screen-reader stop for the Copy to locale select
cases.finding: The initial captured item is never required to be the Copy to combobox. One unrelated starting stop followed by the overwrite checkbox could satisfy the count of one.
cases.next: First establish that the captured stop has the destination control's name and role, then count stops until the verified next field.

cases.test: should move the screen-reader cursor into every shared popup
cases.title: should move the screen-reader cursor into every shared popup
cases.finding: The helper checks generic captured item words such as Title or Field. Those may appear in background content and do not establish popup-local arrival. Five popup flows also make one failure expensive to diagnose.
cases.next: Use popup-specific names/roles/context without moving focus after opening; preserve representative coverage for both localization and the shared popup implementation.

cases.test: should expose disabled row-menu actions to screen-reader navigation
cases.title: should expose disabled row-menu actions to screen-reader navigation
cases.finding: The fixture only opens Blocks, while the ticket describes both Array and Blocks. Matching either paste or replace and a disabled word in merged item/speech output does not verify each disabled action was reached.
cases.next: Check the reported variants and named disabled items in the current cursor output; browser nonactivation assertions remain complementary.

cases.test: should keep the disabled Group by sort control in screen-reader navigation
cases.title: should keep the disabled Group by sort control in screen-reader navigation
cases.finding: The reported disabled control is an AT-discoverability issue, but the helper can match the prior spoken phrase as well as current item text. The actual successful run did reach Sort; the assertion can be more precise.
cases.next: Require the current cursor item to identify Sort and its role/state. Keep the existing Close-button anchor and small step budget.

cases.test: should announce rich-text upload and relationship filter options in NVDA browse mode
cases.title: should announce rich-text upload and relationship filter options in NVDA browse mode
cases.finding: Explicit NVDA browse-mode switching and open-option checks are appropriate. The scan accepts option names anywhere in the next option-count-plus-eight stops, so coincidental background text can satisfy a name.
cases.next: Keep both rich-text drawer types and controls; verify bounded option-list traversal and option context for each required name.

cases.test: should expose relationship option names in NVDA browse mode
cases.title: should expose relationship option names in NVDA browse mode
cases.finding: navigateToWebContent in the installed NVDA adapter clicks the body and resets to page top. Calling it after opening the list can dismiss/change the menu, and Example post can match content outside the intended option list.
cases.next: Establish browse mode without losing the open list; assert it stays open and verify the reported option names within that context.

cases.test: should announce filter and bulk-edit options by name
cases.title: should announce filter and bulk-edit options by name
cases.finding: The test derives an expected active option from the real filter/bulk-edit UI and captures keyboard movement to it. Blank spoken option names are not established solely by DOM names.
cases.next: Keep focused NVDA evidence for all reported control types; confirm whether the failing report is browse- or focus-mode specific before adapting it.

cases.test: should announce both rapid toast messages
cases.title: should announce both rapid toast messages
cases.finding: Two rapid spoken notifications are a timing-dependent AT outcome. Browser tests prove both remain in the native live region but not that both are announced.
cases.next: Retain only if both announcements are the intended product requirement; distinguish screen-reader coalescing/capture loss from product message loss rather than retrying blindly.

cases.test: should announce the unsaved Copy to locale toast without its close button
cases.title: should announce the unsaved Copy to locale toast without its close button
cases.finding: This reproduces the actual unsaved-change toast from the ticket and tests Close toast leaking into spontaneous speech. aria-live=off on a button alone does not prove the announcement.
cases.next: Keep the real-product-flow speech test; do not require the close button to be hidden or inaccessible.

cases.test: should announce the trash toast and dismiss it after the default timeout
cases.title: should announce the trash toast and dismiss it after the default timeout
cases.finding: The test intentionally asserts timed dismissal without putting the virtual cursor on the toast, whereas PYLD-3580 requires persistence while the reader is focused on it.
cases.next: Keep timing/announcement evidence clearly separate; reproduce the cursor-persistence requirement before claiming a remedy or changing production behavior.

cases.test: should announce global API depth changes while focus stays on the stepper
cases.title: should announce global API depth changes while focus stays on the stepper
cases.finding: The spoken assertion accepts any occurrence of the updated number, which can also occur in positional/context speech. Browser checks already prove the numeric value and stable keyboard focus.
cases.next: Require the depth-update message/value context in the spontaneous announcement, while retaining focus on the increment/decrement control.

cases.test: should announce table search result changes without moving focus
cases.title: should announce table search result changes without moving focus
cases.finding: Successive queries can produce the same count. The DOM checks include each query, but the speech regex only requires a generic result count and can accept stale or unrelated count speech.
cases.next: Require result speech tied to the current query as well as count, particularly the two different one-result searches.

cases.test: should announce navigation folder search results without moving focus
cases.title: should announce navigation folder search results without moving focus
cases.finding: The real folder-search submission and resulting count are captured while focus and URL remain stable; this addresses an unsolicited result announcement.
cases.next: Keep; inspect actual speech and live-region update before interpreting a capture failure as a product bug.

PYLD-3580.source: Claude browser-only investigation at commit 54318ef0c7; Playwright WebKit, real trash flow, pointer outside toast, no Guidepup.

observations.closeButtonFocusedDismissal: Approximately 6198ms despite focus being held; activeElement became body.
observations.resumeAfterBlur: Not measurable: focus never paused the timer.

PYLD-3580.rootCause: In installed Sonner 1.7.4, the dismissal timer pauses for expanded/interacting or optional document-hidden state. Focus handlers update restoration refs but do not update pause state.
PYLD-3580.implementationBoundary: The branch deliberately registers a pnpm patch for Sonner 1.7.4. This fixes the development/test checkout, but must be replaced with a distributable dependency solution before publishing the Payload UI package.
PYLD-3580.status: Temporary branch-local Sonner fix passes four focused Chromium regressions and the four reported WebKit browser scenarios. Actual VoiceOver toast navigation remains the outstanding manual check; replace the root patch before the final PR.
PYLD-3580.manualAT: Virtual-cursor-only persistence remains unverified; DOM focus is not equivalent to the VoiceOver cursor.

browserRegression.result: Reproduced: the focused Close toast button and its toast disappear after the default timeout.
browserRegression.command: PORT=3001 MONGODB_URL=<isolated test database> pnpm test:e2e a11y --grep 'should pause trash-toast dismissal while its close button has keyboard focus' --workers=1
browserRegression.failure: The initial toast visibility and Close button focus assertions pass. After seven seconds, the required toast visibility assertion fails because the toast has been removed.
browserRegression.branchState: Included in WCAG.e2e.spec.ts with the temporary dependency fix; previously reproduced the defect and now passes.

logic: Track the focused HTMLElement independently of pointer hover and swipe state.
Pause timers while pointer expansion or keyboard focus is active.
Clear keyboard focus state only when focus leaves the toast list.
Clear stale focus state after a focused element is removed, so subsequent toast timers resume.
temporaryFix.beforePR: Abstract/remove the root pnpm patch and establish a fix that ships to published-package consumers.

browserFixVerification.scope: Pause/resume on DOM keyboard focus, hover leaving while focused, focus movement between toast controls, manual dismissal and subsequent timers, close-button keyboard access, default unfocused dismissal.

criteriaAssessed: 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable (A): focused timeout behavior only; no complete criterion claim
